A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboMirror, and their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 includes supplementary Sections 6–9; the complete supplied v4 ends with references and omits that supplement. This is an identifiable document omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion reconstruction and tracking experiments, ablations, simulator comparisons and real-robot demonstrations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v4 retains original reconstruction, tracking and ablation results in Tables 1–5, and adds motion-video alignment measurements in Table 1.

M1.justification: The Qwen3-VL, flow-matching motion reconstructor, residual MoE teacher and diffusion student pipeline remains unchanged, including its main objectives and inference procedure. Removing supplementary implementation descriptions does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Nymeria egocentric and Motion-X third-person data, evaluate in IsaacGym and MuJoCo, and report Unitree G1 deployment. The omitted supplementary examples do not establish different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 removes the ExBody2 and GMT tracking comparison from v1 Table 11, the PHC/GMR comparison in Figure 5, and the diffusion-versus-MLP comparison in Figure 6. Vid2Mot, ViMo and the main-text ablation comparators remain. The removal substantially narrows evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation design loses the supplementary denoising-step sweeps, sampling-strategy controls and prediction-objective comparisons. v4 adds MV-R@3, MM-V and DTW measurements for Motion-X. Retained experiments keep the stated splits, sampling rates and main model settings; no rerun is established. Foot skating is announced but has no reported Table 1 entry.

E4.justification: v1's DDIM latency sweep, deterministic/stochastic sampling comparison, student and reconstruction objective ablations, retargeting failure analysis and diffusion-versus-MLP cases disappear with Sections 8–9. The main VLM, alignment-versus-reconstruction and pose-versus-latent ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding. v4 adds Motion-X MV-R@3, MM-V and DTW results, including 72.3, 6.24 and 0.23 for RoboMirror. However, v1 Tables 11–15 and additional qualitative findings, including detailed real-robot demonstrations, are removed.

T1.justification: Main flow-matching and diffusion equations remain equivalent. The omitted supplement removes auxiliary mathematical definitions for stability filtering, soft joint limits, curriculum updates and reward terms, including Equations 3–8 and Table 10. Neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain retargeting-free video-to-locomotion, reconstruction-based conditioning, egocentric capability and improved tracking efficiency. The abstract and introduction retain the same 80% latency-reduction and 3.7% success-improvement claims; added measurements do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 omits supplementary explanations of initialization-related failures, GMR distortions motivating PHC selection, and diffusion's ability to avoid reproducing poor reconstructed motions. The main interpretations concerning reconstruction, semantic grounding and retargeting latency remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 loses detailed observation dimensions and histories, optimizer and network specifications, randomization ranges, reward weights, curriculum settings and retargeting choices. Deployment details such as Jetson Orin NX, 50/500 Hz control rates and communication latency also disappear. These are substantial losses of reproducibility information, not demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: v4 adds a RoboPerform discussion and citations including RoboForge, RoboRefer, RoboTracer, SAPAVE, RoboBrain 2.5 and DTW. Appendix-specific references such as PHC, GMR and DDPM disappear. The principal positioning against pose-based tracking and language-driven control remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main sections retain their order and largely identical prose. Local edits update authors and affiliations, metric terminology, related-work text and captions, and add acknowledgements. The supplement is omitted rather than integrated into the narrative, leaving unresolved references to appendix details.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a substantially different visual template, with a boxed title/abstract, changed typography, relocated figures and a widened Table 1. Supplementary Tables 6–15 and Figures 5–10 disappear. Rendering also reveals a broken Figure ?? reference and a flow-matching equation overlapping the adjacent column.

improvement.justification: The added video-motion measurements provide useful evidence, but v4 removes extensive reproducibility specifications, independent tracker comparisons, diagnostic ablations and detailed real-robot demonstrations while retaining broad performance and deployment claims. This substantially weakens reproducibility and evidential support. The limited measurement additions do not offset those losses, especially with unresolved appendix references and unreported foot-skating results.
